refutations.evidence: Range A is the top part of the game's VDP1 command-list buffer, so it is not free RAM. The base table at 0x06047D1C holds three buffers: 0x060E1000 (the command list), 0x060E8000 and 0x06100000. The command list is filled upward through the write pointer 0x060CE668. Appenders at 0x060112F4, 0x0601F030, 0x0602AB86 and 0x0602E9F4 (which steps +32 per command) store commands without comparing the pointer to any limit. No literal anywhere in 0x060E2000-0x060E7FFF appears in CYBER.BIN or any overlay; the only upper bound is the next buffer, 0x060E8000. Each frame, 0x0600FF7C-0x0600FF8C computes size = *0x060CE668 - 0x060E1000 and calls 0x0603D22C(0x25C00000, 0x060E1000, size), which copies the list to VDP1 VRAM 0x0000+. At 0x0600FF90-0x0600FF98 the game stores its own high-water mark of that size in 0x06047D30. In local/opt001/wramh_27173.bin (the frame-27173 Options-screen dump) 0x06047D30 = 0x2300, the 0x8000 end marker is at 0x060E32E0, and the last non-zero byte in the buffer is 0x060E32E0. The largest list seen therefore ran to 0x060E32FF (280 commands of 32 bytes). Its 32-byte end-command slot is 0x060E32E0-0x060E32FF, so the transfer already read the first 28 bytes of A (0x060E32E4-0x060E32FF). These reads were invisible to the breakpoint logs, which log only master SH-2 accesses. The canary only catches writes, and VDP1 ignores everything after the end bit. A's lower bound is exactly this observed peak (0x060E32E0 + 4), not a structural limit. Other dumps show smaller peaks: 0x13E0 in the ending and cast-roll dumps (end001 ck-final-a/b, end010 cast-ram), 0x1300 in end001/dumps/00008042, 0xA20 in loc001/ram3070.

Coverage gap: any scene that draws more than 280 VDP1 commands in one frame writes commands upward from 0x060E3300, over code placed in A. If the command list passes the 0x060E32E0 end slot, the game then sends that code to VDP1 as sprite commands. No appender has a bound check (see the other A entry). The dynamic evidence covered one arcade route that ended in game over, endings entered by RAM writes from checkpoints, and one cold-boot versus fight. The endings were forced, not fought into, so the final and boss fights before them, and the busiest effect and projectile scenes for other mechs, were never run. For example, in M2CB06/M3CB06 record 55 of table A has byte +9 = 0xD0, unlike every other mech's records. Other untested sprite-heavy cases are both players firing projectiles in 2P versus and the attract demos (STDEMO.CMN/MAP). The cast roll stayed at 0x13E0. A safe upper limit for the list is 0x060E8000, where buffer 1 starts. Every load to 0x060E8000 (BUP library and work at 0x06036824 with r4=0x060E8000 and r5=0x060EC000; SDDRVS1.TSK at 0x06032B16; CONTI_0.BIN, 55,456 bytes, at 0x06034EE0) writes upward and does not reach A. If A is used at all, it must leave room for the command list to grow.

Neither table below reaches C with the disc's data. The first runs up to C. Code at 0x060256D4-0x060256EC reads a byte from 0x06054424 + 32*row + (rand & 31) with no bounds check. Row = hit-record byte +13 or +14 (copied from table-A bytes +9/+10 by the 8-byte copy at 0x06025120) plus either 10 or player word +0x190. Word +0x190 is a level: from table 0x0604B0F8 (max 0x1F) or from the upper half of 0x060CFEF8, which 0x06026C1A clamps to 0x001F0000. Rows 128-159 of this table are exactly C (0x06055424-0x06055823). Scanning every mech file's descriptor table A, bytes +9/+10 are 0-2, except M?CB06 record 55 (+9 = 208), which gives rows 208-239, past C. So rows 128-159 are never reached, but nothing in the code stops it. The second table overlaps C's last 12 bytes. Descriptor 0x06057044 in CYBER.BIN = {0x06055824, 0x06056824, 0x06057024, 0x0605702C, 0x06057034; counts 0x100, 0x100, 1, 1, 2}. Every M2CB*/M3CB* mech file stores a pointer to it at object +52 (for example M2CB00A at 0x060734A0-0x060734AA). Its table A (256 records of 16 bytes) starts at 0x06055824, so 0x06055824-0x0605582F, the last 12 bytes of C, are record 0. The four readers of descriptor +0 (0x060250DC, 0x060251B4, 0x060251FC, 0x06026650) all skip index 0 with tst/bt (for example at 0x060250C2, 0x060251B0, 0x060251E2 and 0x0602664C), so record 0 is never read. Ending C at 0x06055824 (1,024 bytes) removes the overlap.

(5) Coverage gap. The breakpoints logged only master SH-2 reads; SCU DMA reads are invisible to them. This is how the A command-list transfer was missed.
